common_name: Navajo White Autumn Sage (White-Flowered Salvia greggii, Navajo Series)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Navajo White is part of the Navajo series of Salvia greggii selections, bearing lightly fragrant pure white flowers that emerge from distinctive chartreuse buds on a tidy, rounded, semi-evergreen to deciduous subshrub from late spring through mid-fall. Like other Salvia greggii cultivars it is exceptionally drought- and heat-tolerant once established, thriving on lean, well-drained soil, and draws bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds throughout its long bloom season. Cut back hard to 6-8 inches in late winter to promote fresh, dense growth and abundant flowering, and shear lightly after each flush to keep the plant tidy.

common_name: Navajo Rose Autumn Sage (Magenta-Rose Salvia greggii, Navajo Series)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Navajo Rose is a compact, free-flowering member of the Navajo series of Salvia greggii selections, covering its tidy rounded form in clear magenta-rose, two-lipped flowers set off by dark calyces from spring into fall. It is a reliable hummingbird and native bee plant and, like other Salvia greggii cultivars, is highly drought- and heat-tolerant once established, needing only occasional deep watering. Cut back hard to 6-8 inches in late winter to renew growth and keep the plant dense and floriferous, and shear lightly after each bloom flush.

common_name: Radio Red Autumn Sage (True Bright-Red Compact Salvia greggii)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in average, dry to medium-moisture, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Plant in average, dry to medium-moisture, well-drained soil in full sun; sandy or rocky soils with sharp drainage are ideal. Radio Red is a compact, well-branched Salvia greggii selection prized for true, bright red, tubular flowers on terminal spikes that hold their vivid color longer than many older red cultivars, blooming from late spring through fall. Its dense, rounded habit makes it useful for borders and mass plantings, and it is highly attractive to hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies while remaining deer resistant. Like other autumn sage selections it is drought-tolerant once established and benefits from a hard cutback in late winter to maintain a tidy, dense form and maximize bloom.

common_name: Pink Preference Autumn Sage (Vivid Purplish-Pink Salvia greggii, Black-Calyx Selection)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in dry, well-drained soil in full to mostly sun.

directions: Plant in a dry, well-drained site in full to mostly sun. Pink Preference is a long-cultivated central Texas selection of Salvia greggii that forms a woody clump topped with vivid purplish-red flowers highlighted by a nearly black floral calyx, blooming most heavily in spring and fall with a steady lighter show through summer. It ranks among the most winter-hardy of the Salvia greggii cultivars and is a dependable hummingbird and beneficial-insect plant. Highly drought-tolerant once established and deer resistant, it benefits from a hard cutback in late winter to renew growth and keep the plant compact and heavily flowering.

common_name: Royal Bumble Salvia (Scarlet-Red Baby Sage with Near-Black Calyces, RHS AGM)

planting.note: Plant in lean to moderately fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light dappled shade.

directions: Royal Bumble is a vigorous baby sage selection holding the RHS Award of Garden Merit, valued for vibrant scarlet-red flowers set off by almost-black stems and calyces against small, glossy, aromatic green leaves. It blooms nearly continuously from late spring through fall (and into early winter in mild climates), giving three seasons of color and drawing bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds in steady numbers. It tolerates coastal conditions and light dappled shade better than many Salvia greggii cultivars while remaining highly drought-tolerant once established. Cut back hard in early spring to remove winter-damaged growth and encourage compact, floriferous new growth.

common_name: Amethyst Lips Salvia (Bicolor Violet-and-White Baby Sage)

planting.note: Plant in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Amethyst Lips is a bushy, upright baby sage selection ('Dyspurp') producing two-toned, two-lipped flowers that are white at the base and broadly banded in rich amethyst-violet at the tips, occasionally appearing solid violet in cool, overcast weather. Its small aromatic leaves have purple-tinged edges and a blackcurrant scent when brushed. It flowers continuously from early summer to autumn, drawing bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds to sunny borders, gravel gardens, and containers. Drought-tolerant once established, it benefits from a hard cutback in early spring to keep growth dense and encourage the heaviest flowering.

common_name: La Trinidad Pink Salvia (Trinity Mountain Sage, Shocking-Pink Baby Sage)

planting.note: Plant in rich, well-drained soil in full, hot sun; established plants tolerate reflected heat well.

directions: La Trinidad Pink, also sold as Trinity Mountain Sage, was discovered in the Sierra Madre Oriental of Nuevo León, Mexico, and forms a wide, long-blooming clump of shocking bright pink flowers that take on a violet cast in cooler weather. It blooms nearly nonstop from spring to fall on fine, deep-green aromatic foliage and is a strong hummingbird and bee attractant. It is heat- and drought-tolerant once established and, being hardier than many baby sage selections, can survive brief dips into the low 20s F. Cut back in early spring to remove winter dieback and keep the wide-spreading clump dense and productive.

common_name: Heatwave Blaze Salvia (Compact Dark-Crimson Greggii-Microphylla Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to dry soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: Heatwave Blaze is part of a Salvia greggii x microphylla hybrid series bred in Australia for extra heat and drought tolerance, forming a compact, rounded, aromatic evergreen shrub covered in masses of dark crimson, two-lipped flowers from spring through fall. It attracts bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds and is deer resistant. It performs best with an occasional deep watering during the growing season despite tolerating extended dry spells once established. Prune once or twice a year to remove spent flowers and refresh growth, which prolongs the bloom period and encourages repeated reflushing.
